Chapter 105: 0102 A Capitalist Gazes at a Lamppost (Bonus chapter for Alliance Leader Mad Bomber)

Over at the Yuan Huo Animation Club, Chen Guiliang was constantly pushing for progress, but the original art for Sanguosha still wasn't finished.

Chen Guiliang planned to hire two more programmers.

Guo Feng gave him a list of part-time salary rates for Peking University students:

Basic development: 30–50 yuan/hour.

Complex development: 50–100 yuan/hour.

Project outsourcing: 1000–3000 yuan, for a development cycle of about 1–3 weeks.

Internship position: 800–1500 yuan/month, requires being present in the office every day, low technical skill required, but the work is easy, and you can slack off to read or write papers.

After reading this list of part-time salaries, Chen Guiliang was filled with endless emotion: Peking University students are so expensive!

Damn it, it was only 2004.

Chen Guiliang had the two of them each hire an assistant. The technical skills didn't need to be great, just enough to do basic development.

Guo Feng continued to develop the campus network. As a shareholder, he wasn't taking a salary for the time being.

Dong Qianqiu was developing the online version of Sanguosha. He still had to wait for the art assets, so he would get the other things done first. His monthly salary was 5000 yuan, higher than a junior programmer in Beijing, but lower than the salary a Peking University graduate would get at a major domestic company.

The two part-time programmers were paid an hourly wage at the median market rate.

At the same time, Chen Guiliang also contacted a nearby restaurant to deliver meals on time. Then he contacted a barbecue stall owner to deliver barbecue once every weekend.

He also hired the cleaning staff from the Peking University Science Park to come and clean once every half a month, paying them per visit.

Over the weekend, Chen Guiliang bought a bicycle and personally rode it to buy a few pots of green plants.

The company sign was also ready and was hung on the door of the small office.

On the third weekend of October, the incubation project manager, Wang Kai, after a phone call with Chen Guiliang, made a special trip to their place for a look around.

"Not bad, it's starting to look like a proper business." Wang Kai stood in the hallway with his hands behind his back, carefully examining the two signs.

Chen Guiliang smiled and said, "It's all thanks to the strong support of Mr. Wang and the Science Park."

Wang Kai said, "Serving the entrepreneurial faculty and students of Peking University is our duty. When can we see some preliminary results from your two projects?"

"In another two weeks, the campus network will be able to enter the final testing phase," Chen Guiliang said. "As for Sanguosha, the artists are still working overtime on the drawings."

Wang Kai walked to the doorway, careful not to disturb the programmers, and nodded in approval. "Your execution is very strong."

He was eager for Chen Guiliang's project to become a success. Promotions and raises aside, the biggest benefit was in the investment stage. Although he wasn't the one who would directly contact venture capital firms, this was a project he was responsible for, and he could still get a cut when it passed through his hands.

After asking about a few more details, Wang Kai returned to his own office and cheerfully filled out the project tracking record.

In the blink of an eye, it was the end of October.

The group from the Yuan Huo Animation Club spent a full 50 days before finally getting the original art done, and they even designed the packaging for the physical card game along the way.

Finding a printing factory was easy.

The printing industry in Beijing was very prosperous, with most factories concentrated in the suburbs like Daxing, Tongzhou, and Shunyi.

Chen Guiliang used his weekends to go from place to place to discuss business.

The first place he found was a printing factory under the Beiyin Group, where a supervisor surnamed Liu met with him.

After Chen Guiliang stated his requirements, Supervisor Liu quoted a price: "25 yuan per set."

"Isn't that too expensive?" Chen Guiliang didn't even want to negotiate.

"We can give you a two-yuan discount if you print a large quantity," Supervisor Liu said. "You're asking for coated paper and lamination, which costs 15 yuan a set for materials alone. Custom rounded corners on the cards require a separate mold, and the die-cutting costs 5 yuan a set. Then there's the box and the instruction manual..."

Supervisor Liu went on for a long time, so Chen Guiliang asked directly, "How much of a discount for an initial print run of 5000 sets?"

Supervisor Liu thought for a moment. "An initial run of 5000 sets would be considered a major client. Mass printing can spread out the costs, so I can knock another 5 yuan off each set for you."

Chen Guiliang then asked to see some of their previous samples.

As expected of a subsidiary of a large state-owned enterprise, the quality was top-notch, but the price was just too high.

Chen Guiliang said he would think about it and then hurried off to other printing factories.

The smaller factories were cheaper, but Chen Guiliang felt their quality was too poor.

After running around for two consecutive days, he finally found a suitable one, a private printing company called Wenboliao.

The quality was no worse than the Beiyin subsidiary, and it was only 13.8 yuan per set, with a required minimum first run of 5000 sets. They also promised to deliver the goods to the Peking University Science Park for free.

The total printing cost was 69,000 yuan.

Private enterprises were very flexible, working overtime to make money. They also dared to slash their prices, offering a quote much lower than the state-owned factory.

When he went to inspect the goods and pay the final balance, Chen Guiliang skipped half an afternoon and a full evening of classes.

What student entrepreneur doesn't skip class?

The newly printed cards were still warm as the workers rapidly packaged them.

After confirming there were no issues, Chen Guiliang stood there, waiting for the goods to be loaded before paying the final balance.

The medium-sized truck could only enter the area within the 5th Ring Road after 10 PM.

By the time Chen Guiliang personally escorted the shipment to the Peking University Science Park, it was already the middle of the night.

The total volume of 5000 sets of Sanguosha was about 7.5 cubic meters. His company office was too small to store them, so he had to rent a small space in the Peking University Science Park's warehouse.

He had also hired two movers to wait there.

Before Sanguosha became popular, it would be difficult to find wholesale distributors. For now, Chen Guiliang could only do the legwork himself, asking retail stores at major universities to sell them on consignment.

As long as Sanguosha became popular at Tsinghua, Peking University, and the surrounding universities, wholesale distributors would come knocking on their own.

After sleeping in the office for an hour, Chen Guiliang rode his bike back to the dorm with a few sets of Sanguosha.

"Where's Senior Brother Min?" Chen Guiliang asked.

Jiang Junlai was half-asleep. "Probably went for his morning workout? Damn, he has so much energy. I feel like I'm not getting enough sleep every day now."

Chen Guiliang yawned and said, "I'm pretty tired too."

He had managed to take a nap in the truck while escorting the cargo last night, and then slept for another hour after the goods were in the warehouse.

Jiang Junlai got out of bed to get dressed. When he saw the Sanguosha box, his sleepiness vanished and he perked up. "The cards are finally done! Quick, let me open it and see."

"Have a look yourself, I'm going to take a nap." Chen Guiliang lay down directly on his bed.

Forgetting to wash up, Jiang Junlai sat on the edge of his bed and unwrapped a Sanguosha set. The more he looked at the hero cards, the more he liked them.

The characters drawn by the Yuan Huo Animation Club were quite different from the ones in the other timeline. But the basic features were preserved, also drawing inspiration from the CCTV version of *Romance of the Three Kingdoms* and Koei's *Romance of the Three Kingdoms*.

"How much for a set?" Jiang Junlai asked.

Chen Guiliang answered groggily, "Don't touch these, I'm giving them to the school clubs. If you want one, come with me to the Science Park sometime, and I'll give you a set then. When you mention it to others, just say you bought it for 30 yuan."

It was only the basic set of cards, but the price was set at 30 yuan.

The 16.2 yuan profit per set wasn't for Chen Guiliang alone to make.

If he used a wholesale distributor, the wholesale price would be around 18 yuan, and Chen Guiliang would only make 4.2 yuan per set.

As for retailers, it all depended on the negotiation; the consignment fee could be anywhere from 15 to 40 percent.

Once it became popular, things would be easier. He could just hand it all over to a wholesaler and not have to worry about anything else.

"Then I'm going to brush my teeth, wash my face, and go to class." Jiang Junlai put the box back down with some reluctance.

Chen Guiliang slept until mid-morning, woken by his alarm reminding him to go to his remaining classes.

At noon, he called Senior Brother Li and Senior Sister Ao.

Li Hang was the first to arrive. "They're printed already? That was fast!"

"This set is for the Yuan Huo Club," Chen Guiliang said. "I promised you five sets, but you'll have to come to the Peking University Science Park to get them. Hehe, and help me promote it a little, won't you?"

"That's easy," Li Hang said happily. "The more students who play Sanguosha, the easier it'll be for me to find people to play with. Within half a month, I guarantee every member of the Yuan Huo Club will know how to play Sanguosha!"

Chen Guiliang said, "I'll also be releasing an online version later, turning Sanguosha into an online game."

"That's great."

Li Hang opened the box, looking through the cards again and again, feeling a great sense of accomplishment, as a quarter of them were drawn by him.

The guy couldn't wait to take the card game away, making a call as he walked. "Sanguosha has been printed... Right, they gave our Yuan Huo Club a set... Don't dawdle, hurry up and come out to play cards!"

Chen Guiliang leaned against the wall, dozing off.

A few minutes later, Ao Yanchen woke him up. "Why did you ask me to come out?"

Chen Guiliang opened his eyes and smilingly handed her a Sanguosha set. "A gift for your May Fourth Club."

"It's not for me? It's for the May Fourth Club?" Ao Yanchen was a bit confused.

Chen Guiliang opened the box, taught her how to play, and they played two one-on-one matches. "This game also has three-player, five-player, and eight-player modes. It's all written in the instruction manual."

"It's quite interesting," Ao Yanchen commented.

Chen Guiliang said, "Help me promote it in the May Fourth Club, okay?"

Ao Yanchen was silent for two seconds, then grumbled, "You crook!"

"You won't be working for free. I'll give you a set later," Chen Guiliang said.

Ao Yanchen said, "And a barbecue meal!"

Chen Guiliang said, "Deal. Senior Sister Ao, do you have the contact information for the leaders of clubs like the Mountaineering Club, the Loving Heart Society, or the Bicycle Association?"

"Well now, Boss Chen." Ao Yanchen already understood what he was planning.

The Mountaineering Club had the most members, ten times that of the Yuan Huo Club.

The Loving Heart Society was second, but it had a greater social influence because they were involved in public service activities.

The Bicycle Association also had a lot of people, about 600 members.

Chen Guiliang said, "Invite them out for barbecue, my treat. Invite as many clubs as you can."

Ao Yanchen didn't know whether to laugh or cry. "And you say I'm not working for free?"

Chen Guiliang said, "If you want a salary, that's fine too. You can join my company."

"What's the monthly salary?" Ao Yanchen asked.

Chen Guiliang said, "For now, it's only 2000. I don't have that much capital. You'd be responsible for promotion at all the major universities, going from one club to another, and also getting retail stores on and off campus to sell the cards on consignment."

"No commission?"

"There is. For every Sanguosha set sold by those retail stores, I'll give you a 10% commission. You can also get more students to help with promotion. In any case, I'm only giving out a 10% commission in total. How much you take from their cut is for you to negotiate."

"The face of a capitalist."

"Hehe, I'll try to be benevolent, so I don't get hung from a lamppost later."

"I'll just treat it as work experience."

"You'll definitely make money. I'm giving Senior Sister Ao an opportunity to earn. Once our game gets popular, you won't have to run around anymore. You can come work at my company doing other things. When we become a big company, you'll be one of the founding members. If you do well, I can even give you stock options!"

"We'll see about that when the time comes."
